candidates.lesson_subject: NAT64 with DNS64: synthetic AAAA records, IPv4 destination extraction, and the policy/VIP/IP-pool chain
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: DNS64 intercepts an IPv6 AAAA query, resolves the A record, synthesizes an AAAA using the NAT64 /96 prefix plus the embedded IPv4 address; NAT64 policy translates IPv6 source/destination to IPv4 using a NAT64-enabled IPv4 pool and VIP6 matching the synthetic prefix.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: IPv6 host -> DNS64 proxy AAAA query -> upstream A lookup -> synthetic 64:ff9b::/96 AAAA -> IPv6 packet to FortiGate -> VIP6/policy match -> destination and source translation -> IPv4 egress.
candidates.failure_class: Synthetic AAAA absent or malformed; DNS proxy not bound to client-facing interface; VIP6 prefix/range mismatch; NAT64 policy not matched; IP pool lacks NAT64; IPv4 route/return path missing.
candidates.evidence_pattern: Client DNS response shows synthesized AAAA; FortiGate DNS proxy query and DNS64 prefix; VIP6 extip and embedded-ipv4-address; NAT64 policy hit counter/debug flow shows translated destination and source pool address; upstream IPv4 packet capture confirms egress.
candidates.remediation_path: Enable IPv6 and DNS Database visibility; bind DNS proxy to the IPv6 LAN interface; validate system dns64 prefix and synthesis behavior; create VIP6 for the entire synthetic prefix; use a NAT64-enabled IPv4 pool on valid subnet boundaries; match IPv6 source/destination and nat64 policy; confirm route and return path.
candidates.question_fingerprint: Synthetic AAAA vs native AAAA; NAT64 VIP6 prefix match; pool nat64 enablement; policy-hit versus DNS-only success.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: IPv6-only client -> FortiGate DNS64 proxy -> synthetic AAAA -> NAT64 VIP6 and policy -> NAT64 source pool -> IPv4 Internet server.
candidates.nearest_prior_comparison: Prior IPv6 prefix-delegation lessons cover ISP IA_PD and downstream address distribution; no prior lesson covers DNS64 synthesis or NAT64 packet translation.

candidates.lesson_subject: Analytics versus Archive log pipeline: local indexing, HA database-range divergence, and archive-backed rebuild
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Archive stores original compressed log files; Analytics inserts and indexes the same log into a local SQL/ClickHouse analytics database for Log View, FortiView, incidents and reports. HA synchronizes archive logs, while each node builds its analytics database locally from the archive range available at rebuild time.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Incoming log -> raw Archive write -> analytics extraction/indexing -> local query/report; HA archive synchronization -> independent node rebuild using selected start date and available archives -> potentially different analytics ranges and database sizes.
candidates.failure_class: Archive exists but Analytics range is absent; ADOM quota/retention trims source archive; rebuild start dates differ between HA members; archive file roll differences are mistaken for missing logs; analytics database size mismatch is misdiagnosed as HA sync failure.
candidates.evidence_pattern: Compare same device/log type/time window in raw Archive on both nodes; inspect archive oldest/newest timestamps, ADOM quota and retention, rebuild start date, SQL/ClickHouse size and hcache; equal HA status does not prove equal indexed date ranges.
candidates.remediation_path: First compare raw archive files for identical device, log type, timestamp and log IDs; check quota/retention before rebuilding; confirm required archives exist on both nodes; rebuild both analytics databases from the same start date within a maintenance window; do not use database size or rolled-file name equality as the sole HA health test.
candidates.question_fingerprint: Archive synchronization versus local analytics indexing; different rebuild windows; hcache as independent factor; raw-log equality as evidence.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiGate log stream forks into raw Archive and local Analytics index; HA sync arrow only for Archive; two independent rebuild pipelines create potentially divergent query ranges.
candidates.nearest_prior_comparison: Prior FortiAnalyzer lessons cover ClickHouse migration, log forwarding and AI Access Visibility; this lesson is the two-tier Archive-to-Analytics data lifecycle and HA range divergence.

candidates.lesson_subject: MSTP topology protection: region consistency, root guard, BPDU guard, and loop guard roles
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: MSTP maps multiple VLANs to spanning-tree instances within a region identified by region name and revision; root guard rejects superior BPDUs on protected non-root-facing ports; BPDU guard disables edge ports receiving BPDUs; loop protection monitors nondesignated ports for loss of expected BPDUs.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Region identity and VLAN-to-instance map -> IST/common BPDU exchange -> per-instance root/role calculation -> root-guard/BPDU-guard/loop-protection action on configured port -> topology reconverges or port enters protected state.
candidates.failure_class: Region name/revision/VLAN map mismatch; rogue superior BPDU changes root path; access port receives BPDU; nondesignated port stops receiving BPDUs; protection feature enabled on wrong port role.
candidates.evidence_pattern: MSTP region name/revision and instance mapping; port role/state; Root-Inconsistent or BPDU-guard timeout/disabled state; BPDU counters and topology change; verify the port is not the root port before applying root guard.
candidates.remediation_path: Map VLANs to instances consistently across the region; choose root bridge deliberately; enable root guard only on ports that must not lead to root; enable BPDU guard only on STP-enabled edge ports; enable loop protection on nondesignated ports; verify recovery timer/manual reset behavior before changing production ports.
candidates.question_fingerprint: Superior BPDU versus any BPDU; root-inconsistent versus edge-port shutdown; loop guard silence; MST region identity and VLAN-instance mapping.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: MST region with core root and redundant access paths; distinct port-role callouts for root guard, edge BPDU guard and nondesignated loop guard.
candidates.nearest_prior_comparison: Prior FortiSwitch lessons cover MCLAG, LACP, routed VLAN OSPF, DNS-over-TLS and FIDO2; no recent lesson covers spanning-tree region/guard semantics.

candidates.lesson_subject: Zero-Wait DFS: pre-cleared backup channels, regulatory-domain modes, and radar-event verification
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Zero-Wait DFS avoids the normal 60-second CAC interruption by maintaining a pre-cleared alternative: rCAC under FCC/MKK pre-scans a backup channel; Pre-CAC under ETSI scans DFS channels in the background and tracks cleared CAC state. Support is hardware/radio/firmware constrained.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiAP profile radio enables zero-wait-dfs -> controller applies profile -> AP pre-scans backup or DFS channel set -> radar detected on home channel -> AP selects a pre-cleared channel -> service resumes without a new CAC when regulatory conditions permit.
candidates.failure_class: Feature configured on unsupported AP/radio/firmware; profile not applied; DFS radar causes channel evacuation; NOL blocks recently detected channels; controller event channel value is misleading; backup/pre-CAC state is not ready.
candidates.evidence_pattern: FortiGate `diagnose wireless-controller wlac -c wtp <serial> | grep zero`; AP `cw_diag -c zwdfs`; `klog | grep Radar`; `rcfg | grep nol`; WiFi event `action=radar-detected`; confirm radio, channel and regulatory domain.
candidates.remediation_path: Confirm supported FAP-U or QCA F/G/K 4x4/8x8 model and FortiAP 7.6.3+; enable zero-wait-dfs under the correct 5-GHz radio profile; apply profile to AP; validate rCAC/Pre-CAC mode and NOL; inspect radar logs and firmware resolved issues; do not interpret a repeated channel ID in a known logging bug as proof that no channel move occurred.
candidates.question_fingerprint: 60-second CAC avoidance versus no-radar guarantee; rCAC versus Pre-CAC regulatory mode; profile applied versus capability; NOL and misleading event channel ID.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiGate WLAN controller/profile -> FortiAP 5-GHz radio -> radar detection -> rCAC backup or ETSI pre-CAC pool -> immediate channel switch and client reassociation.
candidates.nearest_prior_comparison: Prior FortiAP lessons cover CCA threshold tuning, VAP broadcast control and OpenRoaming; this is a DFS radar/CAC pre-clearance mechanism, not RF contention tuning.

candidates.lesson_subject: Persistent Agent upgrade state machine: connect-triggered version comparison, retry counters, and port-80 delivery
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC compares the host Persistent Agent version with the selected target when the agent connects; any version difference can trigger upgrade or downgrade. HTTP port 80 delivers the package; a per-host maximum-attempt counter gates retries; global reset clears counters without re-updating successful hosts.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Host reconnects and agent communicates -> FortiNAC compares version -> package delivered over TCP/80 -> agent installs -> host reports new version -> success/failure event and retry counter update.
candidates.failure_class: Host offline or agent not communicating; TCP/80 blocked; max-attempt counter exhausted; endpoint rollback software restores old agent after reboot; downgrade option/target selection conflicts with endpoint compliance agent version.
candidates.evidence_pattern: Host agent icon/green state and Send Message test; TCP/80 reachability; host current/target versions; Agent Update Failure event; attempt counter; AgentUpdate log shows needsUpdate and updateAttempt; post-reboot version proves persistence.
candidates.remediation_path: Verify the host is online and agent communication works before resetting counters; allow TCP/80 to FortiNAC; inspect host and target version numbers; disable endpoint rollback software; confirm compliance policy target; reset counters only after correcting cause; test a small host cohort before global rollout.
candidates.question_fingerprint: Version differs vs newer-only comparison; TCP/80 package path; max attempts versus reset counter; update success versus reboot rollback.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiNAC agent-update controller -> connected endpoint version check -> TCP/80 package transfer -> install/reboot -> success/failure event and bounded retry counter.
candidates.nearest_prior_comparison: Prior FortiNAC-F lesson covers Persistent Agent certificate validation; this is software update trigger, package transport and retry-state behavior.

candidates.lesson_subject: Dynamic Address Tags: REST API logon/logoff synchronization into FortiGate policy objects
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F acts as a Collector Agent and sends endpoint IP, group and firewall-tag data to FortiGate over REST API; FortiGate maintains dynamic address objects used by source/destination policy matching. Logon triggers include registered connect, user logon, IP change and device status; logoff includes user logoff/disconnect.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiNAC learns registered endpoint and identity -> policy/tag assignment -> REST API logon event to FortiGate -> dynamic address object maps endpoint IP -> firewall policy matches -> logoff/disconnect event removes mapping and policy match.
candidates.failure_class: Wrong integration method/port; FortiNAC not authorized as Security Fabric member; competing FSSO agents overwrite same endpoint IP; REST/API connectivity failure; stale logon remains until timeout; VPN syslog or agent MAC mapping incomplete.
candidates.evidence_pattern: FortiNAC logon/logoff event and endpoint IP/group/tag; FortiGate dynamic address list and View Matched Addresses; connector status and REST API path; VPN syslog RemoteAccess object; SSO debug and 300-second collector-disconnect expiry boundary.
candidates.remediation_path: Choose one integration method consistently: connector-based FSSO tag for non-Fabric or Dynamic Address Tag for Fabric; use the correct port and authorization; avoid multiple agents reporting the same IP; verify logon, IP-change and logoff messages; confirm policy object membership changes before testing traffic; inspect VPN/syslog and Persistent Agent MAC mapping separately.
candidates.question_fingerprint: Connector-based FSSO versus Dynamic Address Tag; registered versus rogue/offline host; logoff removal; one-agent-per-IP and 300-second collector loss.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Endpoint/VPN -> FortiNAC-F registration and identity collector -> REST API Dynamic Address Tag -> FortiGate dynamic IP object -> firewall policy; logoff removes address mapping.

candidates.lesson_subject: Certificate revocation services: local/imported CRLs, OCSP responder publishing, and FortiGate client configuration
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAuthenticator can import CRLs from external authorities, create a local CRL for its own CA, publish revocation status and answer OCSP queries. A revoked end-entity certificate remains represented in CRL until expiry; OCSP uses a responder URL and selected certificate.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: CA issues end-entity certificate -> certificate revoked -> local CRL updated or external CRL imported/downloaded -> relying party retrieves CRL or sends OCSP request -> certificate status controls authentication/TLS acceptance.
candidates.failure_class: CRL/CDP unreachable or stale; wrong issuing CA/CRL association; OCSP URL/port or responder certificate mismatch; certificate chain trusted but status check fails; revoked certificate cannot be deleted before expiry.
candidates.evidence_pattern: Certificate Management CRL entries and issuer; event ID 10121 import success/error; CRL last-update/next-update and download status; FortiGate OCSP server URL and certificate reference; client handshake/revocation result. A trusted chain does not prove certificate is unrevoked.
candidates.remediation_path: Confirm issuer and certificate serial match the CRL; ensure CDP/OCSP endpoint resolves and is reachable; import or publish the correct CRL; configure FortiGate OCSP server with FortiAuthenticator responder URL and TCP/2560 as documented; retain revoked entries until expiry; validate using known-good and known-revoked certificates.
candidates.question_fingerprint: Certificate chain validation versus revocation status; local CRL versus imported CRL; OCSP endpoint reachability; delete-disabled revoked cert lifecycle.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: CA/CRL source -> FortiAuthenticator CRL store and OCSP responder -> FortiGate/client relying party -> certificate status decision.
candidates.nearest_prior_comparison: Prior FortiAuthenticator lessons cover SHA-1 removal, SCEP, FSSO and RADIUS; this is the revocation publication/validation plane, not certificate signing or enrollment.

candidates.lesson_subject: Cross-platform configuration migration: private-data-encryption portability, platform identity, and secret capacity
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiPAM encrypts stored passwords/private keys with a predefined or custom private data encryption key; custom key is 32 hexadecimal characters and is required on another FortiPAM to restore encrypted data. Cross-platform migration requires disabling private-data-encryption on the source before export, preserving product identity and compatible firmware, and ensuring target user-seat capacity.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Source FortiPAM -> disable PDE if cross-platform migration requires it -> create backup -> adjust platform identifier only as documented for supported target type -> restore to same product type and compatible firmware -> verify license/user capacity, secrets and integrations -> re-enable approved encryption posture.
candidates.failure_class: Target cannot decrypt secret fields; product-type mismatch (FortiPAM vs FortiSRA); insufficient user-seat capacity; platform identifier mismatch; firmware version mismatch; custom key lost or inconsistent across HA members.
candidates.evidence_pattern: Backup header platform/build identifier; source/target product type and firmware; private-data-encryption state/key custody; restore warnings; user-seat/license count; sample secret decryption/launch and certificate/private-key use after restore.
candidates.remediation_path: Confirm supported same-product migration and exact source/target firmware; preserve a pre-change backup; follow the documented source PDE disablement before cross-platform export; modify platform identifier only for the documented target mapping; validate user capacity; restore in a maintenance window and verify representative secrets, private keys, launchers and audit data before cutover.
candidates.question_fingerprint: Same product type versus platform type; PDE key dependency versus disabling PDE for cross-platform migration; user-seat capacity; restore success versus usable secret decryption.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Source FortiPAM encryption/key boundary -> backup artifact and platform header -> target FortiPAM compatibility gates -> restore -> secret/key validation and application cutover.
candidates.nearest_prior_comparison: Prior FortiPAM lessons cover ordinary backup/restore and auto-provisioned user lifecycle; this lesson isolates cross-platform identity and private-data-encryption portability.

candidates.lesson_subject: Collector High Availability: VRRP VIP ownership, leader/follower priority, and Supervisor job redistribution
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Collector HA group uses VRRP with one Leader and one or more Followers on the same network as the VIP; highest-priority eligible Follower takes VIP after Leader node failure; Supervisor redistributes event-pull and performance-monitoring jobs across available Collectors.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Configure same-org Collector group -> assign Leader/Follower roles and priorities -> bind VIP to Leader -> send logs to VIP -> Leader node failure -> VRRP ownership moves to Follower -> Supervisor reassigns jobs -> recovered node returns as Follower.
candidates.failure_class: VIP/Collector not on same subnet; multiple/no Leader; priority ordering wrong; VRRP node-level failure not triggered by process-only failure; load balancer health differs from VRRP; stale Collector health metric misread as no ingestion.
candidates.evidence_pattern: Cluster Config test and saved roles; `cat /etc/keepalived/keepalived.conf` virtual_ipaddress; `ip a` confirms VIP on interface; Collector Health last update/last file received/EPS; `phstatus`, `df -h`, `tcpdump -ni any udp port 514`, phoenix.log and Analytics event presence.
candidates.remediation_path: Place VIP and Collectors on the same network; select exactly one Leader and higher priority than Followers; test VRRP configuration; verify VIP ownership and packet arrival after failover; confirm Supervisor job redistribution; distinguish process health and EPS telemetry from actual packet/event ingestion before restarting services.
candidates.question_fingerprint: VRRP node failure versus process failure; VIP ownership versus Supervisor job placement; EPS N/A versus no event ingestion; same-network requirement.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Log sources -> VRRP VIP -> Leader Collector with Follower takeover; Supervisor distributes pull/monitor jobs across the Collector HA group.
candidates.nearest_prior_comparison: Prior FortiSIEM lessons cover Supervisor/PostgreSQL HA and ClickHouse event integrity; this is Collector-edge ingest continuity and VRRP VIP ownership.

candidates.lesson_subject: Split DNS and DNS redirection: domain-selective internal resolution through SPA with Public/Private access type
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSASE forwards endpoint DNS to the service and applies implicit rules for external domains plus split-DNS/domain-specific redirection rules for internal domains; Access Type Public uses PoP WAN egress, Private routes query through SPA to internal DNS, with PoP DNS override for regional resolvers.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Endpoint DNS -> FortiSASE DNS policy lookup -> domain match -> choose internal DNS rule -> Access Type selects public WAN or private SPA path -> internal DNS answer returned through PoP -> endpoint resolves private FQDN.
candidates.failure_class: Private DNS configured as Public so query exits WAN; internal DNS unreachable behind SPA; missing private-access policy for DNS; loopback-BGP source mismatch; DNS filter blocks local domain; DNS-over-TCP selected against unsupported resolver.
candidates.evidence_pattern: Split DNS domain match and primary/secondary DNS; Access Type; SPA BGP design and route; private-access policy for UDP/TCP 53; DNS redirection rule hit; Community scenario confirms loopback source and TLS TCP/853 dependency.
candidates.remediation_path: Create explicit split-DNS rule for internal suffixes; set Private only when DNS server is reachable via SPA; verify BGP route and PoP source path; allow DNS to server in Private Access policy; add URL/DNS filter exception if Newly Observed Domain blocks it; use resolver supporting TCP/853 when selecting DNS-over-TLS.
candidates.question_fingerprint: Public PoP WAN versus Private SPA path; split DNS versus all-domain implicit rule; loopback-BGP source path; DNS filter versus routing failure.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Remote endpoint -> FortiSASE PoP DNS rule engine -> Public WAN DNS lane or Private SPA/BGP hub -> internal DNS server -> response to endpoint.

candidates.lesson_subject: TWAMP Performance SLA probes: active measurement protocol selection, participants, timeout and link-state decisions
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Performance SLA combines health-check probe mode/protocol/server, participating SD-WAN member interfaces, SLA latency/jitter/loss thresholds and link status; TWAMP is a CLI-selectable active probe distinct from ordinary ping and may be absent from GUI protocol choices.
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiGate sends TWAMP probe on each configured participant -> receives TWAMP response -> calculates RTT/jitter/loss -> evaluates SLA targets -> link status changes -> failed member routes are removed from load-balancing group only when all configured health checks fail.
candidates.failure_class: Probe protocol/target mismatch; TWAMP responder unavailable; wrong participant/source interface; probe timeout below real path RTT; health-check interval or SLA thresholds inconsistent with WAN behavior; manual ping succeeds but SLA probe remains dead.
candidates.evidence_pattern: `diagnose sys sdwan health-check` per member with state/loss/latency/jitter; `exec ping-options interface` and ping are only reachability comparison; packet capture confirms TWAMP request/response; inspect probe-timeout, interval, participants, server and protocol.
candidates.remediation_path: Use CLI to configure `set protocol twamp` where required; confirm the target supports TWAMP and replies on the selected path; include only relevant SD-WAN members; tune probe timeout/interval to measured RTT without hiding loss; validate SLA status and route membership after each change.
candidates.question_fingerprint: ICMP ping versus TWAMP SLA; active versus passive mode; all-health-checks-fail removal rule; 500-ms timeout false-dead condition.
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiGate SD-WAN member links -> TWAMP server/responder -> measured RTT/jitter/loss -> SLA thresholds -> link status -> SD-WAN route/load-balance group.
